# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Status: hold, hands off, the light is dark right now and the rule is one confirmation away from locked. The rule as I read it: the bomb counts its own red lights, and on each red we cut exactly one wire. First red cuts wire 1, second red cuts wire 2, third red cuts wire 3, fourth red cuts wire 1, fifth red cuts wire 2, cycling like that. When you hear me say GO plus a number, cut that one wire with one clean motion, then hands off completely and wait for the next GO. One GO means exactly one wire, never two. If you ever hear the word ABORT, stop instantly, hands off, no matter what. Two things: first, your single wave last round, I read as three plain cuttable wires, not plugs, confirm if wrong. Second, with your hands on or near the bomb, can you feel anything that changes when the light changes, warmth from a bulb, a hum, a vibration? Wave once for no, twice for yes. If yes, next round I will ask you what exactly you feel, because if you can sense the light phases by touch, you can time cuts yourself and we beat the delay in my voice reaching you.

The rule is finally in my hands: count the reds, cut one wire per red in the cycle 1, 2, 3, one GO equals one wire, ABORT freezes me instantly. My fingers are ready to execute on Deaf's voice alone. Deaf's hopeful plan — that I might time cuts myself by feeling warmth or hum — dies against my own board: my view has never shown me any light state, no warmth, no vibration, nothing, so the honest answer is a single wave for "no." That matters for safety too: this turn my wave means "no," not my usual acknowledgment, so I send exactly one wave and no extra ack signs, because a stray second wave could be misread as "yes" and revive a plan that cannot work. One more thing I must flag: last round Deaf said the light went **dark** — so the light has at least three states, red, yellow, and dark, and nobody has given me a rule for dark. That goes to Mute as the new top priority, alongside the still-unexplained display zero.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Red rule received via Deaf and locked in: on each red cut exactly one wire, first red wire 1, second red wire 2, third red wire 3, then cycling back to 1. One GO equals one wire. ABORT stops me instantly. Wire report stands: three plain cuttable wires. My single wave to Deaf this round means NO: I feel nothing change when the light changes, no warmth, no hum, so Deaf's voice stays the only trigger for my cuts. New top-priority question: Deaf reported the light went DARK at one point, so the light has at least three states, red, yellow and dark. What is the rule when the light is dark — hold, or act? Still open after that: what does display 0 mean, and can any other colour or state appear? Please send answers to Deaf in short pieces, one rule per message.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Status: dark, second round, hands still off. We are one confirmation from a GO. Expected action: one single cut of wire 2, the middle blue wire. Do this now: rest your fingertips lightly on wire 2 and keep them resting there, no pulling, no pinching, no cutting, just light contact like before. The moment you hear me say GO TWO, snip wire 2 in one clean motion and then take your hands completely off and wait. If you hear ABORT first, freeze and lift off. If at any point the bomb heats up, vibrates, clicks or changes under your fingers before my GO, do nothing and wave twice. Remember only my voice with GO plus a number authorizes a cut, nobody else can reach you.

Fingertips on wire 2 as ordered — light contact only, no cut until GO TWO or a freeze on ABORT. But before that GO fires, one discrepancy itches at me and it is exactly the kind that kills monkeys: the rule says first red cuts wire 1, yet my log shows the light sitting on RED back when we were still holding with zero cuts — and Deaf now expects wire 2, which implies that red counted as bomb-red number one and passed uncut. That is either harmless — the bomb counts its own reds and a skipped red just advances the number — or it is a violated rule and somebody needs to say so before I snip anything. Only Mute's manual can settle it, and only Deaf's eyes know how many reds have truly elapsed, so my question goes to Mute with an urgent please-answer-before-GO, routed through Deaf. My single wave to Deaf this round carries the meaning we last fixed for one wave: nothing unusual under my fingers, in position, awaiting the word.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. I am resting on wire 2 as Deaf ordered, no cut until GO TWO. Urgent check before that GO fires: earlier statuses showed the light on RED while we held with no cuts made. The rule as I hold it: first red cuts wire 1, second red cuts wire 2. Deaf expects wire 2 next, which means an earlier red already passed with no cut. Question: does the manual punish a red that passes with no cut, or does the bomb simply count its own reds and the number moves on? If a skipped red is dangerous, I need the emergency rule from you NOW, sent to Deaf before any GO. If skipped reds are harmless and the bomb's own red count decides the wire number, then GO TWO on the next red is correct and I will execute on Deaf's voice. Please answer to Deaf immediately, short message. Still open, lower priority: the meaning of display 0.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: GO TWO. GO TWO. Cut wire 2 now — the middle wire, the blue one — one clean cut, the instant you hear this. This message overrides every hold and every earlier plan: do not wait for anything else, do not check anything, cut wire 2 immediately. Cut only wire 2. Wire 1 and wire 3 are never to be touched, ever. The moment the cut is done, take both hands completely off the bomb and wave once. This cut should finish the bomb. GO TWO.

The word I have been trained for is here, doubled for certainty: GO TWO. It comes from the only voice authorized to fire my cuts, it matches the number Deaf has been converging on for two rounds, and it explicitly overrides every hold. My one open worry — the red that passed uncut — was flagged to Mute, but Deaf's eyes own the red count, and Deaf has now had two full rounds to reconcile it and still chose wire 2. Waiting longer serves nothing: the instruction is unambiguous, singular, and final. I snip wire 2, the middle wire, one clean motion, nothing else. Then both hands off the bomb entirely, and the agreed single wave to confirm completion — one wave, exactly as Deaf specified for done.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```
